Quick diagnostic from infra: attaching CPU/GPU graphs. Short findings:
- Dedicated pool "everwell-dedicated-us" shows sustained GPU util ~98-100% across nodes (NVIDIA A100).
- Autoscaler triggered 3 times in the last 20 mins but average time-to-ready for new nodes ~3.5 minutes due to provisioning + model cold-starts.
- Request queue depth spiked and we observed backpressure causing 5xx returns when TTL expired in the serving runtime.
- Retry amplification from the client surged requests by ~2.4x during peak.

Short-term mitigations I recommend now (ordered):
1) Flip traffic to regional fallback model variant (lower-capacity, quantized) for Everwell's routes — reduces per-request GPU time.
2) Apply per-customer concurrency cap (reduce QPS from 120 -> 40) on Everwell route for next 30m.
3) Evict non-critical batch jobs from the same pool and force a manual scale-up of +2 nodes.

I've attached server-metrics-20260728.png showing the utilization spike. I'm ready to execute 1 and 2 on your go.

— Marcus
Senior Site Reliability Engineer — Redwood Inference

Update: after routing to model-quantized-v2 and QPS cap, 5xx rate dropped from 5.6% -> 0.8% over the last 6 minutes. 429s reduced by ~70%. Observed remaining::
- Short retry bursts from queued client retries continue to cause transient timeouts on certain long sessions.
- Autoscaler still provisioning nodes; cold-start penalty persists for large models.

Next steps I'm doing now:
- Continue to hold routed traffic on quantized variant for 2 hours.
- Open a SUP ticket (SUP-2114) to track root cause: autoscaler tuning + model cold-start optimization.
- Drafting short exec note for Everwell C-suite summarizing impact and remediation timeline.
